transcript.content: Hello, thank you for coming in. Can you tell me what’s been troubling you or what brings you here today?
I suppose… it’s mostly the worrying. Once it starts, I can’t seem to switch it off, even if I’ve made my list and checked things over and done what I can. It just keeps going.
Do you find that your worrying happens most days and is not just limited to specific situations or events?

Yes… most days, I think. It’s not just one thing. My mind sort of moves from the exhibition schedule, to my daughter’s travel plans, to whether the gutters need looking at… and then small things start to feel like they could turn into something much bigger.
Do you notice that this constant worrying also affects your body, like making you feel restless, tense, or tired easily?

Yes… I do get tense. Even at home, just sitting in the living room, I can feel sort of wound up. I’ll tap my fingers on the phone, or get up and straighten something because sitting still makes me feel… jumpy, I suppose.
Do you feel like you have trouble controlling your worrying, even when you try to focus on something else or remind yourself that things are okay?
Yes… that’s probably the main thing. Once it starts, I can tell myself I’ve made the list, checked the dates, done what I can… but it doesn’t really stop. It just keeps going in the background.
Do these feelings of constant worry and being tense interfere with your daily life, such as making it hard to focus on work, enjoy time with family, or do other things you normally would?

A little, yes. I still do the garden and I go to book club and things like that… but I’m not as prepared as I used to be. And with the exhibition planning, I’ve started saying no to some parts of it because it just feels harder to manage.
How long have you been feeling this way — the constant worrying and being tense — has it been going on for at least six months or more?
Yes… I think it’s been about seven months now. It started not long after my friend died, when I was trying to keep our projects going.
